quizzes.title: Module 1 — Tuesday — Layout & Composition
quizzes.description: Tuesday's quiz covers layout and composition — proximity, white space, alignment, contrast, visual hierarchy and repetition — and how each one shapes the way a design is read.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of proximity in layout and composition?
options: To make every element the same size
To show relationships by grouping related items together
To make the design more colourful
To ensure all elements are placed at the centre
questions.explanation: Proximity is about grouping. Items placed close together read as related, so the spacing between elements tells the viewer what belongs with what.

questions.prompt: A designer notices that a poster looks cluttered and uncomfortable to read. Which adjustment would most likely improve the composition?
options: Adding more decorative elements
Making every text element bold
Increasing the white space between content elements
Removing all margins from the design
questions.explanation: Clutter is usually a spacing problem. More white space between content elements gives each part room to be read, rather than adding more to an already crowded page.

questions.prompt: Why is consistent alignment important in a design?
options: It makes every object identical in appearance.
It helps the composition look organised and easier to navigate.
It ensures that all text is centre-aligned.
It eliminates the need for white space.
questions.explanation: Alignment creates invisible structure. When elements share edges and positions, the composition reads as organised and the viewer's eye moves through it more easily.

questions.prompt: A designer wants an important announcement to catch the viewer's attention immediately. Which technique would best help achieve this?
options: Making every element the same size and colour
Placing all elements close together
Using contrast to make the announcement stand out
Removing the visual hierarchy from the design
questions.explanation: Contrast is what makes one element stand apart from its surroundings. If everything is treated the same, nothing can demand attention first.

questions.prompt: What is the primary function of visual hierarchy in a design?
options: To arrange elements alphabetically
To guide viewers on what to notice first and where to look next
To ensure that every element receives equal attention
To make all sections of a design visually identical
questions.explanation: Hierarchy sets the order of reading. It decides what the viewer sees first, then second, so the message arrives in the sequence you intended.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best demonstrates the principle of repetition?
options: Using a different font style for every heading
Placing unrelated elements next to each other
Using the same colour palette and header style throughout a project
Making the main headline smaller than the supporting text
questions.explanation: Repetition means reusing the same element deliberately. A consistent palette and header style repeated across a project is what ties the pieces together.

questions.prompt: What does white space refer to in layout and composition?
options: Only the areas of a design that are coloured white
The empty spaces between content, lines, and margins
The space reserved exclusively for images
The background of a design when no colour is used
questions.explanation: White space is empty space, not white-coloured space. The gaps between content, lines and margins are what give a design room to breathe.

questions.prompt: A designer creates a poster with several text boxes and images. However, the elements are inconsistently positioned, and the margins differ noticeably across the page. Which principle should the designer focus on improving first?
options: Alignment
Repetition
Contrast
Proximity
questions.explanation: Inconsistent positioning and uneven margins are alignment problems. Bringing the elements onto shared edges and consistent margins is what fixes the untidy structure.
